thread:
samir: FYI support ticket from ACME — saw p99 jump after the variant upgrade that finished ~10m ago. p95/p99 numbers look bad and support is seeing timeouts.

samir: quick metrics snapshot: 
```
model.inference.latency.p50/p95/p99
baseline: 60/210/430 ms
current: 80/480/1600 ms
kvcache.hit_rate: 0.92 -> 0.11
error.rate: 0.2% -> 1.4%
```

samir: rollout_id=rl-2026-07-11-33, variant=redwood-v1.2-int8, tenant=acme-prod (tenant id acme-77).

jess: ugh. do we know if this is global or tenant-scoped? any trace ids?

samir: looks tenant scoped to acme-prod for now; traces attached to the support ticket. sample trace id: trace/0ab9c1f2. spans show high latency inside kvcache.get and a bunch of kvcache.load-miss

aj: possible eviction wave. v1.2 switched allocator flags and kernel selection changed. new allocator can lead to aggressive eviction under bursty loads. can we check eviction logs + kernel container OOMs?

aj: run: `kubectl logs -l app=runtime -c kernel-allocator --since=20m | grep -i evict`

maria: also capture sidecar metrics. if KV hit rate dropped like samir said, that explains p95 balloon (cold KVs hit backend). can someone share a short flame graph or top spans?

samir: pasted short span dump from trace: 
```
span: start->kvcache.lookup (1200ms)
 span: kvcache.load-miss (1100ms)
 span: remote-fetch (900ms)
 span: model.inference.recv (50ms)
```

support-ops: opened a mitigation ticket and pushed traffic split to reduce exposure. currently routing 30% to stable (v1.1) and 70% to v1.2. support ticket #1842 updated.

support-ops: command used: `redwood ctl traffic split --tenant acme-prod --from variant=redwood-v1.2-int8 --to variant=redwood-v1.1 --percent 30`

devops: rolling a hotfix patch that toggles the allocator flag off for the kernel selector in the variant. patch id: patch/alloc-revert-933. deploying to canary hosts now.

devops: config diff (small):
```diff
- kernel_alloc: aggressive_eviction: true
+ kernel_alloc: aggressive_eviction: false
```

maria: good. also request heap/alloc profiles from the kernel container + KV eviction counters. add `--metrics=kv.evictions,kv.hit_rate,heap.alloc` to the debug scrape for the tenant nodes.

aj: we should bisect the variant commit range if hotfix doesn't help. suspects: allocator change (PR #512), batch-scheduler tweak (PR #518), kvcache compaction refactor (PR #521).

oncall-bot: [alert] p99 spike detected for acme-prod (cleared) — auto-alert closed after traffic split.

samir: next steps: 1) collect alloc/eviction metrics + heap profiles (maria & devops) 2) reproduce with synthetic replay at scale (aj) 3) if hotfix doesn't restore kv hit rates, full rollback to v1.1 for acme-prod (support-ops) 4) bisect commits in parallel.

maria: I'll grab profiles and upload to the incident folder. ETA 25m.

aj: I'll start the synthetic replay on a small cluster to try to reproduce the eviction wave pattern — will report back with tracer link.

support-ops: standing by to increase stable traffic if needed. thumbs if OK. :thumbsup:

samir: thanks — keep updates here. tagging @devops @aj @maria for visibility.

samir: quick note for postmortem: log the mismatch between kernel selector decisions and observed cache usage; add a guard in rollout that watches kvcache.hit_rate and auto-halts if hit_rate drops > 25% within 15m.

jess: agreed. long-term we should add a canary workload that mimics tenant hot-paths to catch eviction regressions earlier.

samir: agreed — will add as action item. :white_check_mark:
